newsitem.title: UK: Russia debt prices surge on London Club news.
newsitem.headline: Russia debt prices surge on London Club news.

text.p: Prices of Russian Vneshekonombank debt surged on Friday on news that the country's debt rescheduling deal has been agreed in principle.
Dollar Vnesh debt -- some $35 billion of old Soviet debt which Russia inherited -- was being quoted at 66-1/4 cents in the dollar, its highest on record.
Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov told Reuters in Moscow that the critical mass for creditor agreement on a rescheduling deal had been reached.
Negotiations with the creditors committee were completed earlier this year, though some analysts expect a fairly lengthy process in reconciling the complex trail of ownership of the debt.

The news, already generally assumed in the market, added an extra filip to the price which has more than doubled since the start of this year and has been driving relentlessly higher in the last few days.
By 1300 gmt, it had risen almost two cents and for the moment the market has largely ignored concern over the health of President Boris Yeltsin who is due to undergo heart surgery.
"It's still cheap. I'd buy all the way up to the Eurobond issue, then sell," UBS analyst Alex Mitcheson-Smith said.
He said the price could reach 80 cents and that there were some large holders of the debt targeting the high 70s before they sold.
The latest rise has been sparked by expectations of a credit rating for Russia, possible by the end of this month, for its planned Eurobond issue.
Kasyanov said he expected the $300-500 million bond to be issued late next month or early in November.
Analysts say Russia will probably get around a BB rating.
